Entries.Text: Name rows after what they are linked to: their own text entry, the rows that use them, the rows and text they point at, and project aliases. Useful for modded regulations that come without row names. Generate shows a preview; nothing changes until you press Apply.
Where names may come from. A row's own text entry is tried first, then references (in the order set by Prefer Incoming References), then aliases.

Name these params by a rule of their own instead of the sources below:
AtkParam: the behaviors (player or NPC side), else the bullets that use it.
BehaviorParam: the time act and behavior state (Time Acts and Behaviors).
Bullet: the behaviors that fire it, else the bullets that spawn it.
AttackElementCorrectParam: the scaling that's on, per damage type.
EquipMtrlSetParam and ItemLotParam: the items listed, with counts.
GameAreaParam: the alias of defeatBossFlagId.
Magic: the goods with the same ID.
NpcParam: nameId, else the character alias of the row ID.
NpcThinkParam: the NpcParam row with the same ID, else the character alias.
ResistCorrectParam: the NpcParam fields that use it.
ShopLineupParam: the item of equipId.
SwordArtsParam: the text of textId.
CharaInitParam: the BaseChrSelectMenuParam row that uses it.
AssetEnvironmentGeometryParam: the asset alias of the row ID (1003 = aeg001_003), else no name.
BuddyStoneParam, CutsceneGparamTimeParam, CutsceneGparamWeatherParam, CutsceneMapIdParam, CutSceneTextureLoadParam, MapDefaultInfoParam, MapGdRegionInfoParam, PlayRegionParam, RollingObjLotParam: the map alias of the row ID's first 4 digits (1000 = m10_00).
MapGridCreateHeightDetailLimitInfo: the map alias of currentGridBlockId.
ChrModelParam: the character alias of the row ID's first 4 digits.
MapNameTexParam: the text of mapNameId (a negative ID uses the positive one).
RideParam and ThrowParam: the character aliases of the attacker and defender, e.g. "Player - Torrent".
Start item lot names with the alias of the map their row ID begins with, for IDs of 8 or more digits (10000100 = m10_00, Stormveil Castle), e.g. "Stormveil Castle - Golden Rune [1]".
Use the row's own text entry, such as a weapon or item name, with the same ID as the row.

Name BehaviorParam and BehaviorParam_PC rows after the animation whose time act events use them: the character (or weapon) and the Havok behavior state that plays the animation, e.g. "Crucible Knight - Attack3000" or "Longsword - AttackRightLight1". The attacks and bullets those rows use then take the name through Incoming References. The characters' anibnd and behbnd files are read in the background the first time; unsaved Time Act and Behavior Editor edits aren't included.
Use the name of a row that references this row, e.g. an attack is named after the bullet that uses it. When several rows reference it, the name most of them share is used.
Use the text of the first field that points at a text entry.
Use the name of the first named row this row's fields point at, e.g. an item lot is named after its first item.
Use the project alias of the first field that holds a character, event flag, cutscene, movie, particle or sound ID.
How names are chosen and written.
Only give names to rows that have none. Turn off to replace existing names too.
Run the lookups again so a name generated for one row can name the rows linked to it, e.g. weapon, then behavior, then attack.
Try the rows that reference a row before the rows and text it references. Usually better for attacks, bullets and effects; turn off for item lots and shops.
Add where the name came from, e.g. "Fireball (Bullet)" or "Rune Arc (Item 1)".
Add the animation after the behavior state, e.g. "Crucible Knight - Attack3000 [a000_003000]".
Forget the time acts and behaviors read so far, so the next Generate reads them again. Use after saving changes in the Time Act or Behavior Editor.
Stop reading and don't generate. Characters already read are kept for the next Generate.
